chapter: Chords, recordings and his own groups
title: Leading his own group on 52nd Street; the Blue Note recordings
summary: After Tatum he led a quartet then a sextet with Trummy Young and John Hardee, and recorded Flying Home for Blue Note.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Q. When did you start performing as a leader of your own group.

-- Well I had this little trio, can't even count that, that's not even counted as far as jazz, that little Wynken Blynken and Nod thing. That was a step in the right direction I guess you'd say. But my first little group of my own was right on 52nd St. Right after the Tatum thing broke up. And I got plenty of jobs down there ... Trommy Young, John Herder, Marlow Morris, they were all good players, man. Who else, Jimmy Butts, Al Haig was there. Also Clyde Hart at one time or another. So that was my first thing as far as leading a group. And it was good. We stayed at -- worked at all these clubs -- worked here a while, Famous Door -- all of 'em.
What made you decide to get your own group together?
Now that's a question I don't -- I mean by me hangin' out down there, a guy asked me to have a band, or 'could I get a group together, you know.'

Yeah, Because my name was pretty warm then, just after I left Tatum. So I say yeah, I get a band. We couldn't get nothin' but a little over scale, you know, but a least it was a start for me to get that type of thing started. I had the right guys, you know, fellas could play good, and they knew the type of thing I played, so that's how that started. With 4 pieces, just the rhythm section, no horn. Horns came in later. And John Hardee was in the Army, and he started coming around... And Trumpy Young used to come around and play. So finally the guy hired the whole thing. We had a six piece band. And we made some recordings for Blue Note... Flying Home was one -- oh, those things was fast, the tempos were very fast, but the guys could handle 'em. Even up to now they sound fairly good to me...
